notes: Hiring a car is best (25-40 EUR/day), though KTEL buses run regularly between Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania. Three nights in Chania and two in Heraklion is ideal (the plan uses two bases).

From November to March Samaria is closed, there are no Balos boats (go by jeep) and Elafonisi is deserted. Expect a sunny 15°C winter and the olive harvest; April and May bring wildflowers and Easter.
Knossos costs 20 EUR (museum separate), Samaria 5, Spinalonga 8. Tavernas cost 15-25, with raki offered on the house. Round up the bill as a tip.
Cretan food: dakos, staka, kalitsounia (cheese pastries), snails (chochlioi), tsikoudia. Tap water is drinkable in Chania.
The Balos dirt road voids hire car insurance, so take a boat or a jeep. The ferry and bus back from Samaria arrive late.
Direct flights from Türkiye to Heraklion and Chania run in summer. A Schengen visa is required.

stops.name: Knossos Palace
stops.tips: The palace of King Minos and the labyrinth legend. Arrive for the 08:00 opening, as midday brings heat and tour groups. Note that Evans's restoration is controversial. Book tickets online.

stops.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
stops.tips: Minoan frescoes (the Prince of the Lilies, the Bull-Leaping fresco) and the Phaistos Disc. Air-conditioned.

stops.name: Heraklion Venetian Harbour & Koules
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress and a walk along the breakwater.

stops.name: Peskesi Heraklion
stops.tips: Cretan cuisine: dakos (barley rusk with tomato), staka (creamy dairy spread), wild greens, all farm-sourced.

stops.name: Lions Square & Morosini Fountain
stops.tips: The city centre. Try bougatsa (custard pastry) at Kirkor.

backups.name: Kirkor Bougatsa Heraklion
backups.tips: Serving bougatsa since 1922, with cream filling.

backups.name: Agios Minas Cathedral
backups.tips: The largest cathedral on Crete. An alternative to the harbour.

stops.name: Rethymno Venetian Harbour
stops.tips: On the way (1.5 hours by KTEL bus). Take in the Venetian lighthouse and narrow lanes.

stops.name: Fortezza of Rethymno
stops.tips: A 16th-century fortress with views over the Aegean.

stops.name: Taverna Knossos Rethymno
stops.tips: A family taverna by the harbour. Order the grilled fish.

stops.name: Chania Venetian Harbour
stops.tips: 1 hour by bus. See the Egyptian lighthouse, the Mosque of the Janissaries (Yali Mosque) and the Venetian shipyards (Neoria).

stops.name: Chania Old Town Topanas & Splantzia
stops.tips: The Turkish and Venetian quarters. Walk the leather street (Skridlof) and enjoy the evening lights.

backups.name: Tamam Chania
backups.tips: A restaurant in an old Turkish bathhouse serving Cretan-Ottoman food.

backups.name: Arkadi Monastery
backups.tips: A monastery tied to the 1866 resistance. Detour onto the mountain road from Rethymno (by car).

stops.name: Kissamos Port Balos Boat
stops.tips: No boats in winter. Go by jeep or car on the 8 km dirt road, then a 20-minute descent on foot. It is choppy but completely empty.

stops.name: Gramvousa Fortress
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress on the former pirate island. Expect a 137 m climb and a shipwreck.

stops.name: Balos Lagoon
stops.tips: The winter lagoon is for walking and wind. Swimming is for the brave.

stops.name: Kissamos Taverna Sunset
stops.tips: On the way back, stop at a seaside taverna in Kissamos for stifado (beef and onion stew) and local wine.

backups.name: Falasarna Beach
backups.tips: An ancient harbour and a long beach, ideal at sunset. An alternative to Balos (by car).

backups.name: Cellar Tavern Kissamos
backups.tips: A family taverna in central Kissamos. Lunch here if the boats are not running.

stops.name: Samaria Gorge Xyloskalo Entrance
stops.tips: The gorge is CLOSED in winter (flood risk). Alternatives: Imbros Gorge (8 km, open year-round) or the ancient city of Aptera.

stops.name: Samaria Abandoned Village
stops.tips: An old village halfway along the trail. Rest and refill your water.

stops.name: Iron Gates Sideroportes
stops.tips: The canyon narrows to 3 m here, its tightest point.

stops.name: Agia Roumeli
stops.tips: The coastal village where the gorge ends. Enjoy the sea and a taverna, then take the 17:30 ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, and a bus on to Chania.

stops.name: Chora Sfakion Ferry Return
stops.tips: A ferry across the Libyan Sea, then a bus to Chania, arriving at 20:30.

backups.name: Imbros Gorge
backups.tips: An easy 8 km gorge walk, for when Samaria is closed or too demanding.

stops.name: Elafonisi Beach
stops.tips: The pink sand is empty in winter. Expect a windy walk.

stops.name: Elafonisi Taverna Innachorion
stops.tips: A taverna just behind the beach. Try the Cretan salad.

stops.name: Chrysoskalitissa Monastery
stops.tips: A white monastery perched on a rock, with the legend of the golden step.

stops.name: Topolia Gorge & Agia Sofia Cave
stops.tips: A canyon and a cave church on the way back.

stops.name: Chania Dinner To Maridaki
stops.tips: Seafood meze in Chania Old Town.

backups.name: Kedrodasos Beach
backups.tips: An empty cedar-lined beach next to Elafonisi, a 20-minute walk away.

backups.name: Milia Mountain Retreat Restaurant
backups.tips: Organic food in a mountain village. A detour.

stops.name: Plaka Spinalonga Boat
stops.tips: On the way back to Heraklion, turn east (by car or KTEL). The boat takes 5 minutes from Plaka (20 minutes from Elounda).

stops.name: Spinalonga Island
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress and a leper colony from 1903 to 1957 (the setting of the novel The Island). The walk takes 1 hour.

stops.name: Elounda
stops.tips: A luxury bay village. Try octopus at a harbour taverna.

stops.name: Agios Nikolaos Lake Voulismeni
stops.tips: The legend of the bottomless lake. Cafes and the harbour.

stops.name: Ammoudara Beach Heraklion
stops.tips: A winter beach walk.

backups.name: Kritsa & Panagia Kera
backups.tips: A mountain village with Byzantine frescoes. An alternative to Agios Nikolaos.

backups.name: Ferryman Taverna Elounda
backups.tips: On the set of The Island, by the shore.

stops.name: Heraklion Central Market 1866 Street
stops.tips: Honey, olive oil, raki (tsikoudia), herbs and souvenirs.

stops.name: Nikos Kazantzakis Tomb
stops.tips: The author of Zorba the Greek. His gravestone on the walls reads 'I hope for nothing', with views over the city.

stops.name: Ippokampos Heraklion
stops.tips: A harbour taverna serving calamari and meze. A farewell meal.

stops.name: Heraklion Airport Bus
stops.tips: 15 minutes by bus or taxi. Farewell.

backups.name: Phyllosophies Heraklion
backups.tips: A cafe on the square. Try the cakes.
